summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with secondary progressive multiple sclerosis and neurogenic bladder managed with a chronic Foley catheter, was admitted for weakness, diarrhea, and hematuria. He presented with sepsis from a catheter-associated urinary tract infection, with labs showing leukocytosis, hemoconcentration, and acute kidney injury. He was treated in the ICU with fluid resuscitation and broad-spectrum antibiotics—cefepime and vancomycin—which were continued for 14 days. His hospital course was complicated by a lower gastrointestinal bleed from proctitis, requiring blood transfusions, and hospital-acquired pneumonia, which resolved with treatment. He also developed ileus and severe constipation, managed with disimpaction and a bowel regimen. His oxybutynin was discontinued due to contributing to tachycardia and dry mouth. He improved clinically, with resolution of infection, stabilization of hemoglobin, and return of bowel function. He was discharged home with home health services, a new Foley catheter, and instructions to continue methenamine and vitamin C for UTI prophylaxis, along with a bowel regimen and follow-up for colonoscopy and urology evaluation.
problems: Infection and inflammatory reaction due to indwelling urinary catheter
